reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the webinar promotes an ICO with tokens priced at $10 and tells investors they will receive dividends from the bank's revenue. It frames participation as an opportunity to earn, offers a time-limited token bonus that declines to zero by the fifth week, and directs viewers to subscribe and enter an email to receive links to buy tokens. The speakers also encourage reviewing the product and describe planned documentation, while the records do not establish that the ICO occurred or that the tokens, dividends, or bonuses had value or were paid.

citations.quote: PolybiusBank ICO! Webinar - Everything You Need to Know About ICOs!
1 token costs $10 So, it's $10 with token
We will pay dividend on our revenue!
those investors who supported us, will get money in dividends...
it depends on how much money we collect, it will be already visible to what extent we will build banks, how many clients will we have, etc.

opening.argument: The speakers do not present participation as risk-free or urge viewers to invest without thought. They tell the audience to understand the product and what to expect before committing, and explicitly qualify the project’s scale by saying it depends on how much is collected and how many clients there are. That is a material acknowledgment of uncertainty, not a promise that investors will receive a fixed return. The webinar also says project documents are intended to explain what will be implemented and the investor’s role. These statements do not prove the project sound, but they support reading the pitch as a proposal with contingencies rather than a guaranteed outcome.

citations.quote: You want to get acquainted with a product first
Do not just throw it in your head.
it depends on how much money we collect, it will be already visible to what extent we will build banks, how many clients will we have, etc.
Prospektos will include documents about everything we're about to implement

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution establishes that a token price and proposed dividends were discussed, but those facts alone do not establish a guaranteed return: the speakers qualify the project’s scale and potential income by the amount raised and eventual client base. The declining bonus describes differing token quantities by purchase timing, not a promised increase in token value. And directing viewers toward project materials is consistent with asking them to assess a proposal, not evidence that the proposal was fulfilled or that anyone was deceived.

citations.quote: it depends on how much money we collect, it will be already visible to what extent we will build banks, how many clients will we have, etc.
With every week the bonus will be reduced by 5%.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A caution to study a product does not undo the solicitation around it. The webinar still names a token price, says investors will receive dividends, and advertises an early-purchase bonus. The qualification about funds raised and clients makes the promised scale conditional, but does not change that viewers are being invited to buy into the project on the basis of prospective financial benefits.

citations.quote: 1 token costs $10 So, it's $10 with token
We will pay dividend on our revenue!
We will give him a bonus of 25%

opening.argument: This is structured as an explanatory webinar: the host introduces the topic as what an ICO is, and the guest describes Polybius as a proposed digital-bank concept, including its intended services and business model. The speakers discuss how banking revenue might work and what the project says it plans to build, rather than demonstrating a functioning bank or reporting completed investor outcomes. The audience is also told to understand the product before deciding what to expect. That makes the material reasonably legible as a project presentation and explanation of an ICO, not proof that the claims were realized or that a working investment mechanism was delivered.

citations.quote: Could you please tell us what ICO is?
Polybus bank is our vision of how a bank of the future should look like
You want to get acquainted with a product first
Generally, banking has few source points of income.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats financial discussion as proof of a scam, but the webinar’s stated subject is explaining an ICO and a proposed bank. A token price and discussion of dividends are part of that project presentation; neither establishes that a purchase occurred, that a return was guaranteed, or that the planned bank was represented as already operating. The audience is directed toward further information and told the project’s scope depends on funds and clients, which is consistent with a proposal rather than a report of completed results.

citations.quote: Could you please tell us what ICO is?
it depends on how much money we collect, it will be already visible to what extent we will build banks, how many clients will we have, etc.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the event educational does not change its practical content. The webinar discusses how to buy into the ICO, states a token price, promises dividends from future revenue, and describes a bonus for early participation. Those are purchase-oriented claims, not merely neutral instruction about what an ICO is. The project’s future-tense framing leaves the promised benefits prospective; it does not make the solicitation disappear.

citations.quote: 1 token costs $10 So, it's $10 with token
We will pay dividend on our revenue!
We will give him a bonus of 25%

opening.argument: The material concerns a proposed banking service and a token-based funding offer, which can be assessed as a commercial project pitch without treating every advertised benefit as an established fact. The speakers describe intended digital banking services and acknowledge that the bank’s eventual scale depends on funds raised and clients. The record does not show a viewer making a deposit, surrendering credentials, joining a downline, or receiving a guaranteed return. Even the bonus is described as additional tokens for earlier participation, not as a guaranteed profit or token appreciation. The evidence supports promotional commerce, but does not by itself establish a deceptive mechanism or completed harm.

citations.quote: Everything is supposed to occur on Internet.
it depends on how much money we collect, it will be already visible to what extent we will build banks, how many clients will we have, etc.
We will give him a bonus of 25%
So I bought it for 1000 dollars and I will get tokens for 1250.

rebuttal.rebuttal: A token price, proposed dividends, and a time-limited bonus establish promotion, but not the missing steps needed to establish completed deception: the supplied material does not show a purchase, a payment being taken, or a return being delivered or refused. The early bonus is described as more tokens for the same contribution, not a guaranteed increase in value. The prosecution itself notes that the record does not establish whether the ICO occurred or the benefits were paid; that limitation matters when distinguishing a pitch from proven fraud.

citations.quote: So I bought it for 1000 dollars and I will get tokens for 1250.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The claim is not that the video proves a completed loss; it is that the video promotes token purchases through prospective financial benefits. It gives a token price, ties investor support to dividends, offers extra tokens for early participation, and directs viewers to subscribe for token-purchase links. A completed deposit or credential request is not required to recognize that the content is soliciting investment rather than ordinary retail commerce.
